proposals.before: In the sixteenth year he joined Minister Tang Jinzhao on an investigative tour of Shaanxi and Sichuan to impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and provincial administration commissioner Li Yiwen; both cases went to strict review. When the inquiry into denunciations against Yang was reopened, Wen Qing himself was dismissed.
proposals.after: In the sixteenth year he joined Minister Tang Jinzhao on an investigative tour of Shaanxi and Sichuan to impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and provincial administration commissioner Li Yiwen; both cases went to strict review. When the inquiry into denunciations against Yang was reopened, Yang was stripped of office.
proposals.reason: Chinese 褫其職 after 按名颺被訐事 most naturally demotes Yang Mingyang, and Wen Qing continues acting in the next sentences; the English wrongly makes Wen Qing the one dismissed.

proposals.before: In the sixteenth year, together with Minister Tang Jinzhao he went to Shaanxi and Sichuan to investigate and impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Yiwen; both were referred to strict deliberation. Soon after, upon reinvestigating the matter of Yang Mingyang being denounced, Wen Qing was stripped of his post.
proposals.after: In the sixteenth year, together with Minister Tang Jinzhao he went to Shaanxi and Sichuan to investigate and impeach Governor Yang Mingyang and Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Yiwen; both were referred to strict deliberation. Soon after, upon reinvestigating the matter of Yang Mingyang being denounced, Yang was stripped of his post.
proposals.reason: Same referent error as the idiomatic: 其職 refers to Yang Mingyang, not Wen Qing.

proposals.before: In the eighth month, as the enemy pressed harder, the court fled in haste; Wen Xiang was left as acting chief of the metropolitan gendarmerie to hold Beijing.
proposals.after: In the eighth month, as the enemy pressed harder, the court fled in haste; Wen Xiang was ordered to act as chief of the metropolitan gendarmerie and oversee those remaining in the capital.
proposals.reason: Chinese 司留守 means oversee those left behind; idiomatic invents the place-name Beijing.

proposals.before: In the tenth month, after peace was concluded, he urged the court to return to Beijing so as to steady public morale.
proposals.after: In the tenth month, after peace was concluded, he urged the court to return so as to steady public morale.
proposals.reason: Chinese 回鑾 does not name Beijing; the idiomatic English invents the place.

proposals.before: In the tenth month, on the return to Beijing, he joined the princes and ministers in asking that the two empress dowagers rule from behind the curtain.
proposals.after: In the tenth month, on the return of the court, he joined the princes and ministers in asking that the two empress dowagers rule from behind the curtain.
proposals.reason: Chinese 回鑾 does not name Beijing; the idiomatic English invents the place.

proposals.before: In the eleventh year he was made grand secretary of the Titren Pavilion.
proposals.after: In the eleventh year he was made grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion.
proposals.reason: 體仁閣 is Tiren Pavilion; Titren is a clear misspelling in the idiomatic English.

proposals.before: Wen Xiang stood sternly at court, sternly feared at home and abroad; the court situation relied on him to be maintained and did not change suddenly.
proposals.after: Wen Xiang stood sternly at court and was held in awe at home and abroad; the court situation relied on him to be maintained and did not change suddenly.
proposals.reason: Duplicated 'sternly' and 'sternly feared' are unnatural and obscure the sense of being held in awe.

proposals.before: and though spies were suborned, public outrage was united. On that basis the court was able to accept restraint and secure the present peace.
proposals.after: and though spies were suborned, public outrage was united. On that basis the foreigners could be held in restraint and the present peace settlement was formed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 得受羈縻 takes the foreigners as the restrained party, not the court accepting restraint; the idiomatic subject is reversed.

proposals.before: In the sixth year of Xianfeng Wang Maoyin memorialized on foreign affairs, saying: 'Overseas powers contend daily for dominance; men see a line between China and abroad, but Heaven may see no such distinction.'
proposals.after: In the sixth year of Xianfeng, Wang Maoyin memorialized on foreign affairs, saying: 'Overseas powers contend daily for dominance; men see a line between China and abroad, but Heaven may see no such distinction.'
proposals.reason: Missing comma after the reign date fuses Xianfeng with the personal name Wang Maoyin and obscures the referent.

proposals.before: A warm edict granted condolences, praising him as "upright in conduct, meticulous in statecraft, loyal and pure, bright and straightforward, sincere and fair—a pillar of the realm." He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted a hereditary Captain of Cavalry, inducted into the Shrine of Worthies, given three thousand taels for the funeral, and libations were offered by Prince Zaicheng. He received the posthumous title Wenhong, was buried in Mukden, and General Chong Shi was sent to perform the sacrifice.
proposals.after: A warm edict granted condolences, praising him as "upright in conduct, meticulous in statecraft, loyal and pure, bright and straightforward, sincere and fair—a pillar of the realm." He was posthumously made Grand Tutor, granted a hereditary Captain of Cavalry, inducted into the Shrine of Worthies, given three thousand taels for the funeral, and libations were offered by Prince Zaicheng. He received the posthumous title Wenzhong, was buried in Mukden, and General Chong Shi was sent to perform the sacrifice.
proposals.reason: Posthumous name 文忠 is Wenzhong, not Wenhong; the idiomatic English mistransliterates the established reading.

proposals.before: A warm edict granted condolence gifts, praising him as "upright in personal conduct, meticulous in planning for the state, loyal and pure, bright and straight, sincere and earnest, fair and clear—a minister who is the state's sinews and heart," posthumously appointing him Grand Tutor, granting hereditary Captaincy of Cavalry, induction into the Shrine of Worthies, three thousand taels of silver for the funeral, dispatch of Prince Zaicheng to offer libations, posthumous title Wenhong, burial in Mukden, and ordering General Chong Shi to go and confer sacrifice.
proposals.after: A warm edict granted condolence gifts, praising him as "upright in personal conduct, meticulous in planning for the state, loyal and pure, bright and straight, sincere and earnest, fair and clear—a minister who is the state's sinews and heart," posthumously appointing him Grand Tutor, granting hereditary Captaincy of Cavalry, induction into the Shrine of Worthies, three thousand taels of silver for the funeral, dispatch of Prince Zaicheng to offer libations, posthumous title Wenzhong, burial in Mukden, and ordering General Chong Shi to go and confer sacrifice.
proposals.reason: Posthumous name 文忠 is Wenzhong, not Wenhong; the literal English repeats the same mistransliteration.

proposals.before: In the fifteenth year, when the Empress Dowager resumed power, she recalled his earlier service and granted one altar of sacrifice.
proposals.after: In the fifteenth year, when the Empress Dowager returned power, she recalled his earlier service and granted one altar of sacrifice.
proposals.reason: 歸政 means the Empress Dowager returned governmental power to the emperor, not that she resumed power; the idiomatic English reverses the act.

proposals.before: He was promoted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 內閣學士 is Cabinet Academician/Secretary, not 大學士 (Grand Secretary); the English conflates the two ranks.

proposals.before: He was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.after: He was promoted to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 內閣學士 as Grand Secretary in the literal field.

proposals.before: From early Tongzhi Bao Yun served on the Grand Council, working in harmony with Wen Xiang. He understood government, knew talent, and yielded to the capable; Prince Gong relied on his support. By now, however, the court was dividing into factions.
proposals.after: From the early Tongzhi years, Bao Yun served on the Grand Council, working in harmony with Wen Xiang. He understood government, knew talent, and yielded to the capable; Prince Gong relied on his support. By now, however, the court was dividing into factions.
proposals.reason: Missing comma/wording fuses the reign name Tongzhi with the personal name Bao Yun, creating a false compound reading.

proposals.before: He was thrice transferred to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
proposals.after: He was promoted through three transfers, reaching reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
proposals.reason: 三遷侍讀學士 means three successive promotions culminating in that office, not three transfers into the same post.
